newsitem.title: FRANCE: Pechiney says to begin job cuts in June.
newsitem.headline: Pechiney says to begin job cuts in June.

text.p: French aluminium and packaging group Pechiney confirmed on Monday that it planned to start cutting jobs in France in June.

A company spokesman said Chairman Jean-Pierre Rodier made the announcement during a visit to Brazil last week. Rodier however did not specify the number of jobs to be eliminated nor which plants were concerned.
As part of the Challenge cost cutting plan unveiled last September, Pechiney plans to cut a total of 5,000 jobs worldwide, including 2,700 in France, by the end of 1998.
In France up to 500 jobs are to be cut through redundancies and 1,000 through early retirement. Use of flexible working conditions is to save 1,200 jobs.
Pechiney hopes the Challenge plan will generate cost savings of four billion francs by the end of 1998.
Rodier specified during his trip to Brazil that Pechiney was aiming for a return on invested capital of at least 11 percent for all its sectors in 1999.
Rodier also ruled out a spin-off of its aluminium and packaging businesses, the spokesman said.
